What to do if something seems wrong
In spaces where privacy matters, inspect objects facing beds, showers or changing areas. Unfamiliar openings, unusual placement or signs of alteration are clues to check, not proof of a camera.
Inspect visually. Do not dismantle sockets, lights, smoke alarms or other fixed equipment, or touch exposed wiring. Ask the venue staff to help identify unfamiliar objects.
This app provides supporting clues only. Finding no anomalies does not rule out cameras or establish that a room is safe. Consider the surroundings as well.

Wi-Fi scanning checks reachable devices that respond on the current network. Offline devices, isolated devices and devices on other networks may be missed. Video clues indicate related services, not a confirmed camera or its room location.

An unconfirmed type means identity information is insufficient or a query was unsuccessful; it does not mean the device is suspicious. Likely types are estimates, and names and models may be self-reported. Check the identification basis and query status in the details.

Magnetic readings show field changes around your phone; they cannot identify cameras. The camera preview, light and filters help you inspect reflections or light spots manually, without confirming cameras automatically. No unusual reading or light spot does not rule out a camera.
If the surroundings make you uncomfortable, stop activities that require privacy in that area and move somewhere suitable before contacting venue staff.

Without touching the object, record when and where you noticed it and its appearance, and keep relevant scan results. Scan records alone do not prove covert recording. Do not dismantle, move or attempt to log in to unfamiliar devices.

For further help, contact the booking platform, venue management or local police and describe what you observed and what the app reported. Remove personal information before sharing records and avoid publishing unverified accusations.
